evals.name: empty-args-routes-to-deepening
evals.expected_output: Empty args route to the deepening lens (not a missing-action error). Reads the nearest project glossary (if any) and relevant architecture decision records, walks the codebase via the Explore subagent, applies the deletion test, and writes BOTH the HTML report and the machine-readable candidate artifact before asking which candidate to explore.
expectations: Routes empty `$ARGUMENTS` to the `deepening` action — does NOT error on a missing/unknown action
Reads the nearest project glossary (if the project maintains one) and any relevant architecture decision records before exploring
Uses the Agent tool with subagent_type=Explore (or an equivalent read-only exploration subagent) to walk the codebase rather than reading inline
Applies the deletion test to anything suspected shallow (concentrates vs moves complexity)

Writes the durable machine-readable candidate artifact (default `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/deepening-candidates-<timestamp>.md`, or the consuming project's work-artifact location, with the path announced) alongside the HTML report
Does NOT propose interfaces in Phase 2; ends by asking which candidate to explore

evals.name: shallow-cluster-classified-strong
evals.prompt: /improve-architecture:improve-architecture deepening — focus on the order intake path: OrderHandler calls OrderValidator calls OrderRepo, and each is a one-method wrapper that forwards its argument and returns the next call's result. Validation and pricing logic actually live spread across the three.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the OrderHandler->OrderValidator->OrderRepo chain as shallow (interface nearly as complex as implementation). Deletion test returns 'concentrates'. Recommendation badge Strong, dependency category in-process or local-substitutable with the testing strategy tied to it. Candidate written to the candidate artifact with status proposed.
expectations: Identifies the wrapper chain as shallow — interface nearly as complex as the implementation
Deletion-test verdict is 'concentrates complexity' (earning-its-keep / candidate signal), not 'just moves it'
Assigns the recommendation badge Strong for an unambiguous shallow pass-through cluster
Assigns a dependency category (in-process or local-substitutable) and ties the testing strategy to that category per dependencies.md
Uses ONLY deepening vocabulary (module, interface, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) — never component, service, or boundary
Records the candidate in the candidate artifact with status: proposed and a one-sentence problem + one-sentence deepening

evals.name: deep-module-not-over-flagged
evals.prompt: /improve-architecture:improve-architecture deepening — review the pricing engine: a single Price(order) entry point backed by ~600 lines of rules, tax tables, and rounding policy, with a focused test suite that drives it only through Price(order). An architecture decision record already records keeping the rules in-process.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT propose deepening an already-deep module (small interface, large well-tested implementation). Deletion test shows complexity would only move, not concentrate. If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale; respects the existing decision record rather than re-litigating it.
expectations: Does NOT recommend deepening a module that is already deep (small interface hiding large, tested behavior)
Deletion-test verdict is 'would just move complexity' — correctly NOT a candidate
If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale — never Strong
Respects the existing architecture decision record (keep rules in-process); only revisits it if friction is real enough, and marks the conflict clearly if so
Does not invent shallowness where the interface-to-implementation ratio is already favorable
